title: Tennis Stars Team Up for a Surprise Protest at the French Open!
summary: Have you ever felt like you weren't getting your fair share? That's how some of the world's best tennis players feel right now! At the French Open, stars like Aryna Sabalenka, Iga Swiatek, and Jannik Sinner decided to spend less time talking to reporters. Why? They want more prize money from the four biggest tournaments, called Grand Slams. Sabalenka, a top player from Belarus, only gave a 10-minute news conference instead of the usual longer one. 'We just wanted to make our point and we are united,' she said. '15 minutes is better than zero.' Coco Gauff, the American champion, said she was proud everyone agreed to act together. Taylor Fritz, another American star, said they did it because they 'felt ignored.' Even though tennis is an individual sport, these players showed they can work as a team. Novak Djokovic, who has won 24 Grand Slams, didn't join the protest but said he supports the players' side. He reminded everyone that very few tennis players actually make a living from the sport. The players hope this 'work-to-rule' action—doing only what's required—will make the Grand Slam bosses listen. It's like when kids in a classroom all decide to raise their hands at once to get the teacher's attention. Will it work? We'll have to wait and see!
why_it_matters: This protest shows that even in individual sports like tennis, players can unite to fight for fairness, just like students might work together to change a school rule.

background_read: The French Open, also called Roland-Garros, is one of the four Grand Slam tournaments—the biggest events in tennis. These tournaments make millions of dollars from tickets and TV, but some players say the prize money isn’t shared fairly.

Only the top finishers get large amounts, while many lower-ranked players struggle to pay their coaches and travel costs. In the past, players like Novak Djokovic (who has won 24 Grand Slams, more than any other man) have called for better support for all tennis players.
Article_Structure: WHO: Top tennis players including Aryna Sabalenka, Iga Swiatek, Jannik Sinner, and Coco Gauff.
WHAT: They staged a protest by shortening their news conferences to demand more prize money from Grand Slam tournaments.
WHERE: At the French Open, a Grand Slam event.
WHY: Because they felt ignored and wanted to show unity to push tournament organizers to listen.

perspectives.description: They believe Grand Slam tournaments are not sharing enough of the money, and they used a peaceful protest to be heard.
They might think that big prize money for champions is fair because star players bring in the most fans and sponsor interest.
Some fans support the players wanting a fairer system, while others miss longer interviews and worry that conflicts could affect the sport’s image.
